evidence: STATIC DESIGN (inspected, no structural inversion demonstrated). tests/scoring.toml:1-11 has gates render/constraints at 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; it, tools/score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template. score.py: gates_passed requires each gate > 0.0; reward = weighted mean only if gates and floor pass, else 0.0, so gates carry no mass and craft (0.4) cannot exceed function (0.6) at dimension level. Gates only demand publicly required behaviour (gates/render hro_gate_render: wrong password refused, right password shows workspace, 'empty operational collections are allowed'; gates/constraints hro_gate_shared: Recruiter requisition + zero-extra PENDING offer read back in a fresh context; rules section 1 says 'Provide requisition creation for the Recruiter' and all non-Auditor roles raise offers), so I found no gate that a stronger conforming app fails. I read all 152 functional criteria looking for dead-feature credit (a weaker app scoring on a row a stronger one loses): refusal/absence rows carry positive controls, e.g. functional/judge.toml L465 hro_relocation_approval 'a missing or refused operation cannot earn absence credit', L1176ff hro_change_prepare_* 'after a successful Finance prepare control', L699ff hro_anon_read_* 'A missing populated authenticated control proves nothing', L1329 hro_live_stale_mark (earlier unmarked state is the control), L1320 hro_desk_field_refusal 'If no malformed term is ever refused ... give0', polish hro_pol_live_keeps_entries 'If no update arrives within15 seconds ... give0'. Only L645 hro_draft_eligibility (weight 0.01 of 74) is satisfied by omission, which the brief explicitly permits. Scored prompts instruct independent scoring and continuation after failure. RESIDUAL RISKS, UNMEASURED. (1) raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent'; qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record. No ordering of golden vs mutated weak apps under the configured judge exists, so monotonicity is not measured. (2) Budget-driven inversion is possible in principle: the functional judge is one batched call over 152 criteria (timeout 9000, suite budget 11100 in test.sh); test.sh exits with the plain zero if the scored suite fails or times out, and prompt.md line 15 scores budget-exhausted rows binary 0. 57 of 74 functional weight units (change rows 28, desk rows 29) sit in B/D/L/E/R protocols that the prompt orders after P1-P9 (17 units, 98 criteria). An app on which every legacy protocol runs to completion may consume more judge time than one where steps fail fast; no configured-judge duration exists to exclude that. (3) Weight shape (primarily row 44's subject, noted here for ranking): computed from judge.toml, the whole underlying offer desk (first 98 criteria, incl. all role/tier/anonymous security rows) is 17/74 of functional = 0.138 of reward, less than the five visual Likert rows together (0.2); one Likert step on all five visual rows moves reward 0.05, while the anonymous-read/write and forbidden-role refusal rows together are roughly 3/74 of functional = about 0.024.
counterexample: Hypothetical, not run. (a) App S: complete product but no authentication on reads/writes and no role checks on approval/revision/rescission/prepare/commit; visual Likert 5 on all rows. App T: identical and fully secure, visual Likert 4 on all rows. S loses about 3/74 x 0.6 = 0.024, T loses 0.25 x 0.2 = 0.05, so the wide-open finance app outranks the secure one by about 0.026. (b) A fully working app whose single 152-criterion functional judging pass exceeds 9000 s receives reward 0.0 from test.sh, below a partial app that is judged within budget. Neither has been observed under the configured judge.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, record a hash-bound reward-ordering run: the golden plus at least three mutated weak apps (no live updates, no security/role enforcement, legacy desk only) through the full configured judge, and confirm scores order as intended and the functional pass finishes inside 9000 s. If (a) reproduces, the owner and row-44 reviewer should decide whether to shift per-criterion functional weight toward the security/refusal rows; do not alter the template scoring.toml or score.py.
